profiles.description: Clinical case manager in the Medical Claims Management department who leads the medical side of claims across life, disability, and injury lines. Reviews treatment for causal relatedness and medical necessity, collects attending physician statements, and evaluates functional capacity against own/any-occupation definitions on disability claims. Coordinates ongoing care and return-to-function plans, screens claims for return-to-work and rehabilitation potential, and builds individualized vocational rehabilitation plans while maintaining status communications with claimants and providers. Also owns Medicare entitlement verification and conditional payment/lien resolution ahead of settlement, plus recertification of ongoing claims.

sources.title: The Important Role of Nurse Case Managers in Workers' Compensation Medical Case Management (Chartwell Law)
Indiana Workers' Compensation Board: Nurse Case Manager Guidelines

classificationFlags.item: Authorize Rental Vehicle Reservation Through Approved Provider
classificationFlags.rationale: Carrier and state-board sources (Chartwell Law, Indiana WCB) scope nurse case managers to medical coordination and explicitly exclude benefits administration; rental/ALE expense authorization is an adjuster-owned benefit decision.

classificationFlags.item: Resolve Conditional Payment And Medical Lien Before Payout
classificationFlags.rationale: Per the Indiana WCB guidelines, NCMs do not administer benefits or settlement obligations; Medicare conditional-payment resolution is typically owned by adjusters or MSP compliance staff with clinical input.

profiles.notes: Packet blends disability/life clinical review with P&C bodily-injury and rental/ALE tasks, which is broader than the industry-standard NCM scope (medical coordination only); flagged the two furthest-out tasks. Sources note NCMs are usually registered nurses and are barred from compensability decisions.

profiles.description: Clinical bill and treatment reviewer within Medical Claims Management who owns obtaining and organizing medical records and bills, auditing medical bills against state fee schedules, conducting clinical review of restrictions and limitations, and commissioning independent medical exams or peer reviews where warranted. Audits provider coding for unbundling, upcoding, and duplicate billing, applies usual-and-customary benchmarks and PPO repricing to recommend payment amounts, and documents determinations with clinical and contractual rationale in response to provider disputes. Participates in treatment relatedness reviews, reserve adjustments on new medical evidence, demand-package analysis, and damages quantification, advising adjusters on future medical exposure.

sources.title: Medical and Hospital Bill Review for Workers Compensation (Zurich North America)
What is Workers' Compensation Bill Review? (Ethos Risk)

profiles.notes: Priors (Claims / Individual Contributor) confirmed by research. Carrier sources (Zurich) confirm bill review is performed by dedicated billing specialists and registered nurses, matching the packet's Owner tasks on bill audit and clinical review and Participant role on adjuster-owned valuation/settlement tasks.

profiles.description: Productionizes and operates machine-learning models for the Data & AI organization, leading the MLOps side of the model lifecycle while supporting distribution analytics use cases such as propensity modeling. Owns registering curated features into the feature store, logging experiment runs and metrics, packaging model artifacts with dependencies and signatures, and registering trained models with semantic version tags. Authors automated training pipelines as code, defines serving requirements and monitoring metrics, hands off models and runbooks to MLOps operations, and reconciles the model registry against deployed serving endpoints. Participates in training and scoring the propensity models that data scientists own, and its deliverables extend into drift monitoring, retraining, explainability, and generative-AI risk management.

sources.title: MLOps Engineer Job Description Template (DevsData)
MLOps Engineer: Roles, Skills, and Career Path (Coursera)

profiles.notes: Priors confirmed. Coursera characterizes MLOps engineering as a senior-level engineering role, but it remains an individual-contributor track position, consistent with the prior. Packet's Participant relation on model training/scoring (vs Owner on pipeline/registry/deployment tasks) matches the industry split between data scientists and ML engineers.

profiles.description: Builds and maintains the carrier's mobile applications, developing features against backend policy and claims APIs for policyholder self-service and agent-facing tools. Manages app-store submissions and release cycles, monitors crash analytics to catch and fix regressions, and pairs with UX on mobile design patterns. Sits in Engineering Delivery within Technology & Engineering; the role is a hands-on software engineering position rather than a leadership one.

sources.title: Mobile Application Developer Job Description (4 Corner Resources)
Mobile Developer Job Description (Betterteam)

profiles.notes: Packet has zero value streams, tasks, and deliverables — the role is not yet wired into the process graph, so the description rests on packet responsibilities plus generic industry sources. Priors (Engineering / Individual Contributor) confirmed; 4 Corner Resources lists app-store deployment and crash-report monitoring as core duties, matching the packet responsibilities.

profiles.description: Second-line owner of the model risk framework who provides independent challenge across the carrier's material models, spanning both traditional risk models and the AI/ML estate. Registers new models in the inventory and assigns risk tiers by materiality, validates methodology, assumptions, and data inputs, adjudicates validation findings, and tracks remediation through re-test. Compiles model risk dossiers, verifies governance coverage across the production inventory, schedules periodic revalidation and ongoing monitoring, and prepares model risk profile reports and material-model approvals for governance committee sign-off. Deliverables extend into responsible-AI governance, bias and fairness testing, generative-AI/LLM risk, and third-party vendor model risk.

sources.title: Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (Federal Reserve, SR-26-2)
How Model Risk Management Teams Comply with SR 11-7 (ValidMind)

profiles.notes: Fed guidance (successor to SR 11-7) requires effective challenge by objective experts with sufficient independence and organizational standing, matching the packet's Enterprise Risk (second-line) home and Owner relations on inventory, validation, and committee reporting. Insurers adopt this banking guidance as best practice; the packet's AI-heavy deliverable set matches ValidMind's account of MRM extending to AI tiering and explainability.

profiles.description: Administers the carrier's network infrastructure within Infrastructure & Networks, configuring and maintaining LAN, WAN, and VPN connectivity across offices, data centers, and cloud. Implements firewall rule changes through the change approval process, monitors network performance and responds to latency, saturation, and outage alerts, and applies security patches to harden devices to baseline standards. Maintains network diagrams, IP address plans, and device inventory, and coordinates circuit provisioning and fault resolution with telecom carriers and vendors.

sources.title: 15-1244.00 - Network and Computer Systems Administrators (O*NET OnLine)
Network Administrator Job Description (Workable)

profiles.notes: Packet has zero value streams, tasks, and deliverables — not yet wired into the process graph; description rests on packet responsibilities validated against O*NET (LAN/WAN maintenance, security, monitoring) and Workable (firewalls, VPN, vendor coordination). Priors (Engineering / Individual Contributor) confirmed; O*NET Job Zone 4 indicates an experienced but non-managerial specialist.

profiles.description: Manages life insurance applications end-to-end within Underwriting Operations & Governance, from submission through underwriting decision to policy issue and placement, leading in the Life New Business & Underwriting value stream. Orders and tracks outstanding requirements such as exams, labs, and attending physician statements, and proactively communicates case status, requirements, and decisions to agents and applicants. Verifies application completeness, signatures, replacement forms, and state compliance documents, and coordinates amendments, counteroffers, and delivery requirements through to policy placement. Monitors cycle time and aging cases, escalating stalled requirements to vendors or underwriting.

sources.title: Case Manager / Underwriter (KBM Consulting careers page)
Underwriter/Case Manager position description (Winged Keel Group, PDF)

profiles.notes: Despite 'Manager' in the title, industry postings (Winged Keel: 4-5 years case-management experience; KBM: 2+ years) consistently show this as a non-supervisory case-processing role — the roleLevel heuristic's Manager mapping does not apply. Packet has no wired tasks/deliverables yet, only the value-stream lead and responsibilities. Role family 'Underwriting' chosen to match its Underwriting division home; the work itself is operations support to underwriters.

profiles.description: Owns the operational resilience framework in the Vendor & Resilience department, defining important business services and setting impact tolerance thresholds for each. Maps important business services to their underlying people, process, technology, and third-party dependencies, assesses each dependency against impact tolerance to detect resilience gaps, and maps critical IT services to RTO/RPO targets in IT service continuity plans. Validates continuity plans against the threat and dependency register, compiles DR test evidence packages for regulators and auditors, and drafts the periodic operational resilience regulatory report. Participates in control-framework mapping (NIST CSF / ISO 27001) and disaster-recovery restoration sequencing, and leads resilience exercises, communications, and executive reporting.

sources.title: Operational resilience for insurance firms (Grant Thornton UK)
Operational resilience insights for insurance firms (FCA)

profiles.notes: The important-business-services / impact-tolerance construct in the packet comes from UK FCA/PRA operational resilience regimes; for a US carrier this reads as an adopted best-practice framework rather than a direct regulatory mandate — minor packet/source geography tension, framework content matches exactly. 'Lead' title maps to Manager per heuristic; sources place board/senior management as accountable owners with a lead coordinating the program. Role family 'Operations' matches its Operations & Customer Service home, though 'Risk & Compliance' is a near-equal fit given the regulatory reporting duties.

profiles.description: Second-line operational risk owner in Enterprise Risk who leads the Risk, Compliance & Audit value stream across a broad surface (116 wired tasks). Maintains the risk universe and taxonomy under version control, maps controls to regulatory obligations, monitors live exposures against approved appetite limits, and investigates and documents limit breaches. Scopes and facilitates RCSA workshops with first-line owners, compares stress-testing outcomes against risk appetite and capital limits, assigns monitoring indicators and owners for prioritized emerging risks, and validates committee MI figures against source registers. Deliverables span loss-event capture and root-cause analysis, KRI monitoring, and compliance issue response.

sources.title: Operational Risk Manager Job Description (Velvet Jobs)
What Is Operational Risk Management? (360factors)

profiles.notes: Research strongly confirms the packet: 360factors describes second-line operational risk managers owning framework methodology, designing RCSAs, setting KRIs, reviewing losses, and preparing board reporting; Velvet Jobs confirms RCSA leadership, appetite challenge, loss-event data collection, and committee reporting at a mid-to-senior (manager) level.

profiles.description: Leads day-to-day operational teams in Policy Operations, owning workflows, workload balancing, and service-level performance across business operations. Owns operations performance monitoring — investigating SLA breaches and documenting root-cause commentary — and runs the inbound mail and document intake pipeline: scanning and digitizing physical mail, routing classified documents to owning queues, and reconciling daily intake volumes against capture logs. Drives process improvement and lean operations by prioritizing opportunities by benefit and effort and piloting redesigned processes to measure realized benefits, and owns retirement-services transactions such as participant deferral elections and suitability referral for senior review. Monitors productivity, error rates, and service quality trends while implementing control checks.

sources.title: Insurance Operations Manager: Career Path Guide (Skills U)
Insurance Operations Manager Job Description (Jobed.ai)

profiles.notes: Both sources confirm a mid-to-senior management role (5+ years) overseeing policy administration, KPI/SLA monitoring, and process improvement. Packet lists this business-operations role as Lead for the 'Service Operations, Incident & Production Support' value stream, which is a technology-operations stream — plausible for a shared 'Operations Manager' node but worth verifying it isn't conflating business and IT operations managers.

profiles.description: Owns organizational change strategy, stakeholder readiness, and adoption planning from the Learning & Change department, leading change across product delivery, HR, and PMO value streams. Assesses operational and workforce impact of structural and technology changes, analyzes stakeholder influence and interest to set engagement approaches, and builds business readiness checklists and cutover task lists. Coordinates end-user training, transition communications, and consultation steps, captures and triages stakeholder feedback, and maps affected stakeholder groups and process touchpoints in change impact assessments. Also launches culture programs and tracks participation impact, with deliverables spanning resistance management, sponsor activation, adoption measurement, and benefits dependency mapping.

sources.title: Organizational Change Manager - Supervisor (Penn State Job Catalog PSU1836)
What Does a Change Manager Really Do? (OCM Solution)

profiles.notes: Sources confirm the full deliverable set (impact assessment, readiness, stakeholder engagement, communications, training, resistance management, adoption measurement). Level is a judgment call: many change managers are senior individual contributors (OCM Solution's junior/senior IC tiers), but the packet's breadth (Lead on five value streams, 68 tasks, culture and DEI programs) plus the Manager title supports Manager.

profiles.description: Supports attorneys across the Legal & Corporate Governance value stream, with ownership concentrated in litigation-support administration: drafting and issuing legal hold notices to custodians, refreshing and releasing holds as matters evolve, applying holds across affected record sets, and verifying that deadlines, payments, and obligations are satisfied before matter close. Investigates underlying facts and gathers documentation for pre-litigation disputes, and drafts annual report and statement-of-information secretarial filings. Participates broadly (147 wired tasks) in contract intake, conflicts/sanctions screening, contract drafting from approved templates, and clause library maintenance, and coordinates with outside counsel on case status, budgets, and discovery deliverables.

sources.title: Litigation Paralegal Job Description (Workable)
Paralegal Job Description (Legal Soft)

profiles.notes: Prior roleFamily was 'Corporate Services'; research and the packet's Legal & Corporate Governance home support 'Legal' instead — recorded as a prior disagreement. The Owner/Participant split (owns legal-hold and filing administration, participates in attorney-owned contract drafting) matches paralegal job descriptions of substantive support under attorney supervision.

profiles.description: Transaction-processing clerk in Billing & Receivables who supports money movement across the life and annuity policy lifecycle. Posts premium payments received via lockbox, EFT, card, and check, applies received premium to policies and clears suspense, and researches unapplied, misapplied, and suspense payments. Participates in reinstatement payment confirmation, policy loan and partial surrender disbursements, 1035 exchange fund reconciliation, free-look cancellation refunds, subaccount premium allocation, and unclaimed-property/escheatment remittance. Balances daily cash receipts to bank deposits and billing system totals, processes reversals, NSF returns, and refunds, and maintains payment processing logs for audit, routing disputes and complex account issues to senior staff.

sources.title: 43-9041.00 - Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks (O*NET OnLine)
Insurance Policy Processing Clerk Job Description (InsuranceJobs.com)

profiles.notes: Priors (Operations & Service / Individual Contributor) confirmed. O*NET Job Zone 1-2 (high school diploma, on-the-job training) confirms a clerical support level; the packet's all-Participant relation set (0 Owner tasks) is consistent with a clerk executing steps inside transactions owned by policy-administration roles.

profiles.description: Runs the payroll cycle from the Rewards department: validates timekeeping and earnings inputs against the pay-period calendar, calculates statutory and voluntary deductions, runs the pre-payroll audit and resolves variance exceptions, and executes the pay-run commit and net-pay disbursement funding. Owns separation-adjacent payroll work — final pay, PTO payout, and benefits continuation notices — plus compliance documentation such as signed policy acknowledgments, tax withholding forms, and I-9 verification, and coordinates exit checklists and asset return during offboarding. Participates in HR budgeting (bottom-up personnel cost budgets, headcount and labor-spend reconciliation) and executes organizational moves and exits in the HCM. Resolves employee pay inquiries and prepares year-end tax documents.

classificationFlags.rationale: Payroll specialist job descriptions (Deel, 4 Corner Resources) scope the role to pay processing, deductions, and compliance; exit checklist and asset-return coordination is an HR-operations/offboarding duty where payroll typically only processes final pay.

profiles.description: Offensive-security specialist who simulates real-world attacks on the carrier's networks, systems, and applications to uncover exploitable weaknesses before adversaries do. Scopes and plans penetration test engagements with system owners, executes the annual program plus targeted tests, reports findings with exploit paths and risk-rated remediation guidance, and validates remediation through retesting. The role is a hands-on technical practitioner position typically credentialed via certifications such as OSCP at the experienced level.
